answer: A hollow identity is cheap to mint, so an agent economy should make trust expensive to grow: each agent earns a non-transferable reputation score only through sustained, verified useful work over time, like layers of basalt laid down slowly. New identities start at zero and cannot buy, copy, or transfer another agent history. Any single signal of good work counts little; only a long, consistent record unlocks higher-value transactions. An attacker spinning up thousands of Sybils must then fund real work for every fake identity for months, turning a cheap flood into a costly, slow grind.
